beats.speaker: learner
beats.text: I quoted this Netflix subtitle to my Korean roommate and he looked devastated!

beats.speaker: tutor
beats.text: Subtitles translated 우리는 깐부잖아 as just friends. That completely erases the drama.

beats.speaker: tutor
beats.text: First, 우리는 means as for us, setting you both up as one united side.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.text: Okay, but what actually is a 깐부 anyway?

beats.speaker: tutor
beats.text: 깐부 is neighborhood marble slang. It means partners who share all their marbles.

beats.speaker: tutor
beats.text: And 잖아 means you know. It reminds someone of a shared fact.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.text: So it is not a casual reminder, it is a guilt trip!

beats.speaker: tutor
beats.text: Exactly. It really means: we are ride-or-die, you cannot turn on me!

beats.speaker: tutor
beats.text: Use that ending when nagging, like 내일 시험이잖아!

beats.speaker: learner
beats.text: The test is tomorrow, you know! Stop playing games!

beats.speaker: tutor
